title: Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea (low BMI + exercise + lanugo): decreased pulsatile GnRH
vignette: A 15-year-old girl comes to the office with her mother due to amenorrhea. Menarche occurred at age 12, but she has had no menses for the past several months. Her mother also says that the patient seems to have stopped growing and that her 14-year-old younger sister has grown taller than her. The patient's academic activities are unchanged, and she participates in school gymnastics. She has no history of chronic medical conditions. Blood pressure is 110/68 mm Hg and pulse is 75/min. BMI is 16.6 kg/m2. Physical examination shows fine hair on her face and arms. The remainder of the examination shows no abnormalities. Urine pregnancy test is negative. Which of the following is the most likely underlying cause of this patient's amenorrhea?

clues.text: no menses for the past several months
clues.note: Cessation of menses after menarche is secondary amenorrhea; with a negative pregnancy test, evaluate the hypothalamic-pituitary-ovarian axis.
Intensive exercise (gymnastics) with relative caloric deficiency is a common setting for functional hypothalamic amenorrhea.
BMI 16.6 (normal 18.5-24.9) reflects very low body weight/low adipose stores - a key driver of functional hypothalamic amenorrhea.

clues.text: fine hair on her face and arms
clues.note: Lanugo (fine, soft body hair) is a sign of chronic undernutrition, supporting low energy availability as the cause.

whatMatters: Low body weight (BMI 16.6 / normal 18.5-24.9), strenuous exercise, and lanugo indicate FUNCTIONAL HYPOTHALAMIC AMENORRHEA. Reduced adipose tissue lowers LEPTIN, which INHIBITS pulsatile GnRH release -> low LH/FSH -> low estrogen -> amenorrhea. The underlying cause is DECREASED hypothalamic pulsatile GnRH. Answer A.
strategy: Tie the low-energy phenotype (low BMI, athlete, lanugo) to the axis: low leptin -> decreased pulsatile GnRH -> low LH/FSH -> low estrogen (central/hypogonadotropic cause). Reject options implying androgen excess or other mechanisms: decreased SHBG (PCOS pattern - usually higher BMI, hirsutism, not lanugo), increased estrogen->testosterone conversion (not a real direction/mechanism here), prolactin-mediated suppression (prolactinoma - galactorrhea), and neoplastic androgen production (virilization).

eliminations.label: Decreased SHBG - PCOS pattern, not this
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: low sex hormone-binding globulin raising free testosterone (seen in polycystic ovary syndrome). ❌ WHY IT FAILS: PCOS typically occurs with higher BMI and hirsutism (coarse terminal hair), whereas this patient has LOW BMI and lanugo from undernutrition. ✅ Correct if: overweight patient with hirsutism/irregular menses (PCOS).

eliminations.label: Increased estrogen->testosterone conversion - wrong direction
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: purported conversion of estrogen to testosterone. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: aromatase converts androgens TO estrogen (not the reverse), and this mechanism doesn't explain low-energy amenorrhea. ✅ Correct if: (not a real physiologic pathway as stated).

eliminations.label: Prolactin-mediated suppression - prolactinoma
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: hyperprolactinemia suppressing GnRH/gonadotropins. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: it can cause amenorrhea but usually with galactorrhea; the low BMI/exercise/lanugo picture points to functional hypothalamic amenorrhea instead. ✅ Correct if: amenorrhea + galactorrhea + elevated prolactin.

eliminations.label: Neoplastic androgen production - virilization
eliminations.detail: WHAT IT IS: an androgen-secreting adrenal/ovarian tumor. ❌ WHY IT FAILS: those cause virilization (voice deepening, clitoromegaly, rapid hirsutism) with high androgens, absent here. ✅ Correct if: rapid virilization with markedly elevated testosterone/DHEA.

reasoning: Low BMI + intensive exercise + lanugo = low energy availability
Low leptin inhibits pulsatile GnRH -> low LH/FSH -> low estrogen -> amenorrhea
-> decreased hypothalamic pulsatile GnRH secretion; answer A
mechanism: FUNCTIONAL HYPOTHALAMIC AMENORRHEA occurs with low energy availability - very low body weight (as in anorexia nervosa) or intense exercise with relative caloric deficiency (e.g., gymnasts, distance runners). Diminished ADIPOSE tissue reduces circulating LEPTIN; low leptin (with other stress signals) INHIBITS the pulsatile release of GONADOTROPIN-RELEASING HORMONE (GnRH) from the hypothalamus. Reduced GnRH pulsatility lowers pituitary LH and FSH secretion, producing low circulating ESTROGEN, ANOVULATION/amenorrhea, and reduced peak bone mass (a hypogonadotropic, central cause). Supporting features here include low BMI, participation in gymnastics, and LANUGO (fine body hair of chronic undernutrition). Management centers on restoring adequate energy availability/weight. The distractors fit other conditions: decreased SHBG with free-androgen excess (PCOS, typically higher BMI/hirsutism), hyperprolactinemia (galactorrhea), and androgen-secreting tumors (virilization) - none of which match this low-energy presentation. (Because chronic undernutrition and eating disorders are involved, evaluation should be compassionate; the National Alliance for Eating Disorders is an appropriate support resource if an eating disorder is suspected.)

difficulty.label: 🧠 Knowledge
difficulty.text: First Aid Repro/Endo > functional hypothalamic amenorrhea: low energy availability (anorexia, athletes) -> low leptin -> decreased pulsatile GnRH -> low LH/FSH -> low estrogen; amenorrhea + low bone density; lanugo in undernutrition.

difficulty.label: 📖 Comprehension
difficulty.text: Low BMI + exercise + lanugo -> low leptin -> decreased pulsatile GnRH (central/hypogonadotropic).

difficulty.label: 🔤 Vocab
difficulty.text: Unsure on pulsatile GnRH, leptin, hypogonadotropic hypogonadism, lanugo, or functional hypothalamic amenorrhea? Tell me which.

difficulty.label: 🨤 Distractor
difficulty.text: Low SHBG/androgen excess = PCOS (higher BMI, hirsutism); prolactin = galactorrhea; androgen tumor = virilization.

difficulty.label: 🗒️ Other
difficulty.text: Bank: low energy availability -> low leptin -> decreased GnRH pulsatility -> functional hypothalamic amenorrhea; restore energy/weight.

keywords.back: Decreased pulsatile GnRH (low leptin from low energy availability)
Fine soft body hair of chronic undernutrition
Higher BMI, hirsutism, low SHBG (free androgen excess)

firstAid.detail: Repro: low leptin -> decreased pulsatile GnRH -> low LH/FSH/estrogen.
Endo > PCOS, prolactinoma, androgen tumor differ.

memoryHook: When the body runs on empty (low fat -> low leptin), the hypothalamus stops pulsing GnRH to save energy - periods switch off centrally.
